top_story: A US move to disable a Palau-flagged merchant ship leaving Iran on 27 November sharpened a cycle of action and retaliation around the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran responding hours later by reaffirming its intent to keep the waterway shut and confront the blockade. That escalation raises the risk that commercial traffic and energy flows will face sustained disruption, extending pressure from military signaling into civilian markets across the Gulf. In Israel, a 26 November coalition deal positioning Yair Golan to potentially replace Itamar Ben-Gvir as police minister points to a possible shift in domestic security politics, even as Gaza’s collapsing health system and contaminated water are driving a meningitis outbreak among children. The regional picture is one of tightening coercion on two fronts: maritime confrontation is hardening in the Gulf while governance failures and war damage continue to translate directly into acute human harm in Gaza.
